chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
For everything there is a spring, and the spring of the Quran is the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: What is the spring of the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) employs the metaphor of 'spring' (Rabi') to illustrate that Ramadan serves as the annual spiritual renewal for the Quran, mirroring how nature revives in its respective season. This narration underscores the inseparable bond between the revelation of the Quran and the month of Ramadan, a connection deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition as the time when the Quran's guidance is most actively internalized and practiced by the faithful.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘For everything there is a spring, and the spring of the Quran is a Month of Ramazan’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al- Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
For everything there is a spring. The spring for the Holy Quran is the month of Ramadan.’”
